newsitem.title: USA: Republican chief Barbour blasts U.S. industry.
newsitem.headline: Republican chief Barbour blasts U.S. industry.

text.p: Republican National Chairman Haley Barbour lashed out Monday at industry groups for failing to put up a strong fight for Republicans against the union-led left in the 1996 elections.

"The left, led by the union bosses, ... put its entire arsenal behind electing Democrats," Barbour said at the American Petroleum Institute's annual meeting. "For most of big business, the 1996 election was business as usual. There was no special effort -- giving to both sides."
He said the Business Roundtable "effort hurt Republicans in the end," with the party having losing a net six to eight seats in the House.
Reinforcing calls for campaign finance reforms, Barbour complained about what he called the unions' "bottomless well of union dues."
"Congress must ... prohibit unions or anybody else from taking people's money by coercion," he said.

The American Petroleum Institute shrugged off Barbour's comments at a later press conference. "If you look at the data, the oil and gas industry ... is generally strongly supportive of what Haley was doing," said Exxon chairman Lee Raymond.
